tvShow.name: Prehistoric Planet
tvShow.overview: Experience the wonders of our world like never before in this epic series from Jon Favreau and the producers of Planet Earth. Travel back 66 million years to when majestic dinosaurs and extraordinary creatures roamed the lands, seas, and skies.

episodes.name: Uncovered: Could T. Rex Really Swim?
episodes.overview: They're huge, powerful...and full of surprises.

episodes.name: Uncovered: Flamboyant Flyers
episodes.overview: Why would a flying reptile have a large and cumbersome, yet remarkable, head crest? Learn this and more about Pterosaurs in Prehistoric Planet.

episodes.name: Uncovered: Did Velociraptor Have Feathers?
episodes.overview: “It would've looked a lot more like a really terrifying turkey.” Millions of years later, dinosaurs are still full of surprises.

episodes.name: Uncovered: Did Dinosaurs Hunt in Packs?
episodes.overview: “There is scientific evidence for deadly dinosaurs joining forces.”

episodes.name: Uncovered: Armed for Seduction?
episodes.overview: A tiny pair of limbs with a big role to play.

episodes.name: On Location with Prehistoric Planet
episodes.overview: Real landscapes. Remarkable creatures. An extraordinary team. Watch how the creators of Prehistoric Planet brought this one-of-a-kind documentary to life.

episodes.name: Uncovered: Could Giant Pterosaurs Really Hunt on the Ground?
episodes.overview: Pterosaurs were rare flying reptiles that could both fly through the air and catch prey on land efficiently.

episodes.name: Uncovered: Were Dinosaurs Good Parents?
episodes.overview: When it came to dino eggs, parents had to employ a safety-first approach.

episodes.name: Uncovered: Was Pachycephalosaur Really a Headbutter?
episodes.overview: Finding the purpose for a dome-headed dinosaur.

episodes.name: Uncovered: How Fast Was a Mosasaur?
episodes.overview: Learn more about the secrets of Mosasaurs' underwater success.

episodes.name: Uncovered: Why Did Triceratops Have a Frill?
episodes.overview: There were no frills on the frills of Triceratops.

episodes.name: Uncovered: Uncovered: How Did Dinosaurs Get So Big?
episodes.overview: Prehistoric size had very few limits.

episodes.name: Uncovered: What Do We Really Know About Ammonites?
episodes.overview: Using the present to inform the past.

episodes.name: Uncovered: How Good Were T.rex Senses?
episodes.overview: Super sight, smell, and hearing helped the T.rex hunt.

episodes.name: Uncovered: What Else Lived Alongside the Dinosaurs?
episodes.overview: It took special skills to live alongside dinos.

episodes.name: Uncovered: How Did Ankylosaurs Use Their Tail?
episodes.overview: Ankylosaurus was an early wielder of weaponized anatomy.

episodes.name: Coasts
episodes.overview: A pregnant Tuarangisaurus is in distress—and her young calf can sense it—as she travels waters that are home to the ocean's deadliest predators.

episodes.name: Deserts
episodes.overview: Above the deserts of North Africa, aerial combat ensues as male Barbaridactylus pterosaurs fight for the attention of females below.

episodes.name: Freshwater
episodes.overview: With its feathered body and duck bill, the eight-ton Deinocheirus wades through an Asian wetland in search of relief from pesky biting flies.

episodes.name: Ice Worlds
episodes.overview: Within the snow-covered forest, a tense standoff develops between ancient rivals, Pachyrhinosaurus and Nanuqsaurus.

episodes.name: Forests
episodes.overview: A journey through an underground cave in North America turns perilous when a young Triceratops is separated from its mother.

episodes.name: Islands
episodes.overview: On a small island, a monumental display takes place as the giant Hatzegopteryx reveals his gentler side to woo a mate.

episodes.name: Badlands
episodes.overview: Trudging through a scorching desert, two young Tarchia find relief at an oasis and encounter an adult twice their size, ready to lay claim.

episodes.name: Swamps
episodes.overview: In a drought-stricken basin where much has perished, an old Pachycephalosaurus bull defends his leadership against a young challenger.

episodes.name: Oceans
episodes.overview: Deep beneath the water's surface, the world's largest predator—the Mosasaurus—lies in wait to ambush unsuspecting prey.

episodes.name: North America
episodes.overview: Not many can intimidate North America's top predator, T. rex, whose size and bite are a deadly combo—except for a giant winged foe.

episodes.name: The Big Freeze
episodes.overview: In a world covered in ice, woolly mammoths and saber-toothed cats fight to survive the coldest temperatures in millions of years.

episodes.name: New Lands
episodes.overview: As sea levels drop and continents shift, animals begin migrating to unknown territories full of new possibilities—and new threats.

episodes.name: Desert Lands
episodes.overview: With much of the planet's water supply frozen, rock-climbing sloths and marsupial lions must find a way to withstand barren landscapes.

episodes.name: Grass Lands
episodes.overview: Giant herd animals thrive with the expansion of the grasslands, dominating the plains—but fearsome hunters shadow their every move.

episodes.name: The Big Melt
episodes.overview: Rising temperatures mean every habitat on the planet is transforming, and for the Goliaths of the Ice Age, the world as they know it is ending.

guest_stars.character: Self - Associate Curator, La Brea Tar Pits
guest_stars.name: Emily L. Lindsey

seasons.name: Ice Age
seasons.overview: From towering woolly mammoths to elusive snow sloths, terrifying saber-toothed tigers to resilient dwarf elephants (only 3 feet tall), Prehistoric Planet: Ice Age reveals the epic struggles and unexpected stories of animals that once ruled the Ice Age. Journey through vast tundras, barren deserts, expanding grasslands and melting permafrost as these creatures battle for survival in the face of extreme climates, shifting landscapes and the onset of "The Big Freeze," and ultimately, "The Big Melt."
